hb-01.context: Hebrews speaks to believers tempted to turn back from the faith. Before any command, the author presents who Jesus is: the Son through whom God finally spoke and who is above the angels.
hb-01.focusQuestion: What changes for you knowing that God finally spoke through the Son?
hb-01.keywordGloss: Jesus is not just a messenger of God: he is the Son, heir of everything and above the angels.
facts: Long ago, God spoke to the fathers through the prophets.
In these last days, God has spoken through the Son.
God made the universe through the Son.
The Son sustains all things by the word of his power.
The Son became superior to the angels.

hb-02.context: After speaking of God's rest and the word that exposes the heart, Hebrews presents Jesus as the great high priest who passed through the heavens and knows our weakness.
hb-02.focusQuestion: What keeps you from approaching God with confidence when you feel weak?
hb-02.keywordGloss: Jesus enters God's presence on behalf of his people and sympathizes with the weak.
facts: The word of God is living and active.
Nothing is hidden before God.
Jesus is the great high priest who passed through the heavens.
Jesus was tempted in all things, yet without sin.
At the throne of grace we receive mercy and grace.

hb-03.context: Hebrews compares the service of the ancient priests, a copy and shadow of heaven, with Jesus' ministry. He is mediator of a superior covenant, established on better promises.
hb-03.focusQuestion: Where do you still try to reach God through your own effort, and not through Jesus?
hb-03.keywordGloss: God's agreement with his people through Jesus, with better promises than the old ones.
facts: Every high priest offers gifts and sacrifices.
The ancient priests minister as a copy and shadow of heaven.
Jesus is mediator of a superior covenant.
The superior covenant is established on better promises.
God promises to establish a new covenant with Israel and Judah.

hb-04.context: After calling the people not to turn back, Hebrews defines faith and begins to recall the ancients. Faith trusts what God promised, even without seeing, and acts from that trust.
hb-04.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you need to trust God without yet seeing the result?
hb-04.keywordGloss: Assurance of what is hoped for and conviction of what is not seen, leading us to act in trust of God.
facts: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
By faith, the ancients received a good testimony.
The worlds were formed by the word of God.
Abel offered God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain.
Abel, though dead, still speaks.

hb-boss.context: This review gathers the thread of Hebrews: God spoke through the Son who is greater than the angels, our sympathetic high priest, mediator of the new covenant, and the faith that perseveres without seeing.
hb-boss.focusQuestion: Given everything Jesus is, what do you need to stop putting off with God?
hb-boss.keywordGloss: Keep trusting in Jesus, greater and sufficient, without turning back from faith.
reflectionPrompts: Faith that does not turn back
facts: In these last days, God has spoken through the Son.
Jesus was tempted in all things, yet without sin.
Jesus is mediator of a superior covenant.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
Abel offered God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain.
At the throne of grace we receive mercy and grace.
